item.title: Smoke-free 2040 goal failing as young adults keep vaping
item.description:
Smoke-free 2040 goal failing as young adults keep vaping

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A survey has suggested that four in ten young adults in the Netherlands smoke or vape, pointing to how far the country remains from its goal of a smoke-free generation by 2040.

Under the National Prevention Agreement, the government wants nobody in the younger generation to be smoking or vaping by then, and fewer than 5% of adults to do so.

The 40% figure comes from a poll of 2,000 people by comparison website Independer, which found the habit most common among 18-to-29-year-olds. The share drops to around 30% among people in their thirties, 17% among the over-45s and 10% among the over-60s.

Independer is a commercial comparison site rather than a statistical agency, and its figure is well above official data. National statistics agency CBS put the proportion of 18-to-25-year-olds who smoke or vape at roughly a quarter in 2024.

Doctors want a ban
Paediatric lung specialist Noor Rikkers, of the Artsen slaan alarm (doctors sound the alarm) campaign group, called the numbers shocking and said the rise of vaping was drawing in ever-younger children.

She wants the government to ban all products that contain nicotine, arguing that a blanket ban would be simpler to enforce than the current patchwork of rules.

Social media a factor
The survey also pointed to social media. About three-quarters of young adults said they saw videos of people smoking or vaping, and a third of those said the clips tempted them to try it.

More than a quarter of the young smokers who watched such videos said they bought cigarettes or vapes through social media, even though online and social-media sales of tobacco and vapes have been banned since 2023 – a rule dealers have been flouting on Snapchat.

Flavoured vapes have been banned since January 2024, but doctors and inspectors say a black market keeps supplying illegal products.

item.title: Dutch broadcaster AvroTros to boycott Eurovision again in 2027
item.description:
Dutch broadcaster AvroTros to boycott Eurovision again in 2027

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch broadcaster AvroTros will boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second year in 2027 in protest at Israel’s continuing participation.

The company called in a statement for “transparent rules” on countries involved in military conflicts to restore the “neutrality” of the event.

“It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the contest, undermining its neutral character,” director-general Taco Zimmerman said. “The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division.”

The Netherlands was one of five countries that refused to enter last year’s competition in response to the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, although the contest in Austria was still shown on Dutch TV by public broadcaster NPO.

The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) has since changed its rules to ban winning countries from hosting the following year’s event if they are involved in a “sensitive geopolitical situation” that affects the “security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region”.

But AvroTros said the revision did not go far enough to reassure it that the “independent and neutral character of the Eurovision Song Contest has been restored”.

Humanity

“Participation is therefore no longer consistent with the values of AvroTros: trustworthiness, independence and humanity,” it said.

The new rules are essentially a recognition of existing practice: Ukraine won the contest in 2022, but the following year’s event was held in the UK because of the Russian invasion.

NPO said it would consider whether it would broadcast next year’s song contest, which is being held in Bulgaria.

A spokesman said it was “a great shame” that AvroTros was boycotting the event. “We see that the geopolitical tensions are having a divisive effect. That makes it a difficult decision for our colleagues.”

item.title: Saints and Stars gym chain fined €300k for breaching work rules
item.description:
Saints and Stars gym chain fined €300k for breaching work rules

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Amsterdam gym chain Saints and Stars has been hit with more than €300,000 in fines for breaching Dutch employment laws.

The biggest fine of €234,000 after labour inspectors found it hired 25 non-EU nationals without permits and had failed to check the identity of three staff.

The gym was at the centre of controversy last year when city newspaper Het Parool reported that it forced cleaners from Indonesia and the Philippines to work 17 hours a day and share beds with strangers while working in its four branches.

The exposée prompted several trainers and influencers to cancel their memberships at the €139-a-month gym. Last December a judge awarded five Filipino cleaners €15,000 each in compensation.

The latest fines also included €60,000 for failing to comply with the laws on minimum wage and holiday pay, after inspectors were unable to determine how many hours employees had worked and whether they had received the minimum wage.

The chain was also fined €22,500 for not observing mandatory break times.

The inspectors also issued two official warnings to Saints and Stars, meaning the gyms could be temporarily closed if they breach the rules a third time in the next five years.

The company said it would not appeal against the fines. “This should not have happened,” owner Tom Moos said in a press statement.

item.title: Japanese ambassador attends memorial for Burma railway victims
item.description:
Japanese ambassador attends memorial for Burma railway victims

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Japan’s ambassador to the Netherlands has attended a ceremony to commemorate labourers who died during the construction of the Siam-Burma railway during the Second World War.

It is the first time Michii Rokuichiro has been invited to join the annual ceremony at the Bronbeek estate in Arnhem, where he laid a wreath before a memorial to the victims on Saturday.

Some 3,000 Dutch prisoners of war were among the tens of thousands of Allied soldiers and forced labourers from occupied south-east Asia who perished during the building of the 415km route between Thailand and Myanmar, which became known as the Death Railway.

The organisers of the ceremony said they had extended the invitation “as a sign of recognition and a meaningful step in the conversation about our shared history.” “Fortunately, our supporters were in favour,” said chairman Wouter Neuhaus.

“Nothing can take away the suffering that has been inflicted and the sorrow that the first and subsequent generations carry with them,” the organisation said in a statement on its website.

“But we not that within the community there is a need for reconciliation and dialogue, especially at a time when freedom can no longer be taken for granted.”

“Good for history”

Emmy Janssens, of the Dutch campaign group Stichting Japanse Ereschulden (Foundation of Japanese Honorary Debts), told NOS that not everybody was comfortable with the decision.

“For me personally, it’s acceptable,” she said. “But I can understand if some people find it hard to swallow.”

Ed van de Logt, the last surviving Dutch labourer, who was guest of honour at the ceremony, said the ambassador’s attendance was “good for history”.

“It’s great that they have the courage to come here. It’s very good for history for the two countries to reconcile.”

It is the latest sign of Japan’s growing readiness to recognise the victims of the Second World War in countries it occupied and its treatment of prisoners of war.

The Japanese emperor, Naruhito, laid a wreath at the national war memorial in Amsterdam during his state visit in June, beside an urn representing the victims of the invasion of Indonesia in 1942, when it was a Dutch colony.

The emperor said it was “deeply heartbreaking” that people had suffered “agonising experiences” during the war and acknowledged that people in the Netherlands “even today continue to bear the pain of that time”.

item.title: ING funding oil firms it vowed to drop, report finds
item.description:
ING funding oil firms it vowed to drop, report finds

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

ING has failed on its promise to stop financing oil and gas companies that keep opening new fields, an investigation by Follow the Money (FTM) has found.

In September 2024 the Amsterdam-based bank said it would immediately halt all new financing to companies whose business is exploring for and extracting oil and gas, so-called “pure-play” producers, as long as they were still opening new fields.

It went on to help fund three of them anyway: Norway’s Aker BP and Vår Energi and the UK’s NEO Energy, all of which are pure-play producers.

The general loans and bonds it arranged for the companies through 2025 and into 2026 came to more than $900 million, FTM found. Larger, diversified firms such as Shell, which also refines, transports and sells oil, are outside the pledge and ING can still finance them.

Environmental organisation Milieudefensie, the Dutch arm of Friends of the Earth, called the pledge misleading from the start. Most oil and gas is pumped by exactly those bigger firms the promise did not cover, said Nicky van Dijk, who leads the group’s research for its climate case against the bank.

“They’ve closed off one small loophole,” she told FTM, “and now it turns out they’re not even sticking to that.”

ING’s annual reports show its direct lending is falling: outstanding loans to upstream oil and gas firms dropped from €2 billion in 2024 to €1.4 billion in 2025, according to FTM. But that misses the bond market, where ING still helps these firms borrow – arranging the sale of their debt to investors instead of lending to them directly.

ING told FTM it does not comment on individual clients, and that its policy follows the International Energy Agency’s net-zero scenario, which it said sets no exact definition of a “new” field. But the agency classes any project begun after 2021 as new, FTM said, and found at least one at each of the three firms.

The findings could feed into Milieudefensie’s case against ING, filed in 2024, which demands the bank halve the emissions it finances by 2030. “One investment could still be a mistake,” Van Dijk said, “but three?”.

item.title: Rotterdam council sacks building officials over corrupt payments
item.description:
Rotterdam council sacks building officials over corrupt payments

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two civil servants have been dismissed in Rotterdam for corruption after an investigation found they accepted gifts from contractors working on city building projects.

The sackings were confirmed after prosecutors told the council executive that a fraud investigation had revealed “substantially more serious” allegations than were initially suspected.

The prosecution said a total of 11 people and six companies were implicated in the fraud inquiry. The NRC newspaper quoted sources who said the companies submitted inflated estimates with the help of the civil servants.

One of the officials, a project manager, used a company he set up to support promising young footballers as a slush fund to channel payments from a building firm working on cultural renovations.

After he took early retirement, the prosecution service began investigating allegations that he and a colleague had accepted bribes and forged documents, in breach of the law and the city’s code of ethics.

A third colleague was dismissed at the end of 2023 in connection with the criminal investigation.

Houses and business premises in The Hague, Echt, Capelle aan den IJssel and Nieuwekerk were searched in the course of the inquiry. They include the home of one of the civil servants, who both worked in the City Development department.

Boijmans van Beuningen

One of the projects was the removal of asbestos from the Boijmans van Beuningen museum. An earlier investigation by NRC found that the council had paid at least €3 million too much for the project.

The company that won the contract. Brabant-based A van Liempd, employed four people at the time, only one of whom was qualified to supervise asbestos removal.

The company based its estimate on the assumption that 5.7km of air vents would need to be stripped, but less than half the installation was found to contain asbestos. It also promised to use an innovative technique to contain carcinogenic materials, but carried out most of the work with standard methods, NRC reported.

A lawyer for the company would not comment because of the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Inheritance wave will increase housing inequality, experts warn
item.description:
Inheritance wave will increase housing inequality, experts warn

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A wave of inheritances over the next decade is set to drive up house prices in the Netherlands even further, a report by financial experts has said.

An estimated €300 billion will be passed on by the baby-boomer generation between 2024 and 2023, much of which will be reinvested in property, according to financial advice agency Van Bruggen.

Mortgage expert Oscar Noorlag warned that the transfer of wealth would increase inequality, as the benefits will be mainly felt by the richest households, many of whom are already homeowners.

The cash will allow them to move up the ladder or invest in a suitable retirement home. But at the other end of the scale people living in rental properties will see their costs rise without having a substantial inheritance to fall back on.

In 2024 the richest 10% of households owned 56% of all capital wealth, while the average householder had built up a fortune of €563,000 compared to €40,400 for the average tenant.

“It’s not just income that determines what people do in the housing market,” Noorlag said. “The wealth of people’s parents and grandparents is playing an increasing role.

“But not everyone has access to that family wealth, and that income inequality is threatening to transfer to the housing market.”

Senior housing

Van Bruggen’s advice goes against the common assumption that the housing market cools off as the population ages, because older people are less likely to move up the ladder.

Since the 1970s the proportion of owner-occupied houses in the Netherlands has risen from 35% to 59%, while the 2.3 million people (12.7%) living in social rental housing generally have the lowest incomes and savings.

House prices have risen by 240% since the end of the last crash in the summer of 2013, despite a brief dip at the end of the pandemic and are still rising, although the rate has cooled from more than 10% in early 2025 to 4% last month.

Noorlag said the government needed to prioritise building senior housing so that older people could move out of the homes where they raised their children.

“When older people can move into a suitable home, more houses become available for the next generations,” he said. “That allows for more house moves that the whole market benefits from.”

item.title: Police arrest 14-year-old for impersonating a policeman
item.description:
Police arrest 14-year-old for impersonating a policeman

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have arrested a 14-year-old boy in Zwolle for impersonating a police officer in order to rob the homes of elderly people around the city. The boy, from Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht in Zuid-Holland, was working with an older man from Rotterdam.

A series of reports were made to police in the area about fake policeman knocking on the doors of houses around Zwolle, according to regional broadcaster RTV Oost. At least two houses were burgled with money and jewellery being taken.

The police identified the suspects through CCTV and arrested both of them when they were spotted in a car. The victims have had their belongings returned to them.

Young people posing as police officers is a growing crime, according to local police. A community officer told NOS that youths are being recruited by older people and are simply carrying out orders.

Last month, a 13-year-old from Spijkenisse was arrested for the same crime. He had managed to steal €20,000 worth of jewellery.

The police reported around 500 fake police agent incidents last year, according to news site NU.nl. Almost all follow a similar pattern: they make phone calls or send letters to vulnerable older people telling them there have been neighbourhood robberies and their belongings are at risk.

They then go to their houses under the guise of safeguarding them, before stealing from them.

item.title: Warm week ahead, thunderstorms likely on Thursday
item.description:
Warm week ahead, thunderstorms likely on Thursday

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The week starts warm and sunny across the Netherlands, but is set to break on Thursday with heavy thunderstorms.

Monday brings plenty of sun and highs of 21 to 24°. Tuesday is warmer at 23 to 25° in much of the country, though the southeast is cloudier.

Wednesday turns muggy, reaching 24 to 26° with a rising chance of showers later on. Thursday is the warmest day at 25 to 28°, and close to tropical in the southeast, before heavy showers and thunderstorms move in from the afternoon. Some could be severe, with hail and strong gusts, the national weather service KNMI said.

Friday will be cooler, around 19 to 22° with further showers, and the weekend – the last of the meteorological summer, which ends on August 31 – looks cooler still at about 21°.

KNMI had no weather warnings in force as of Sunday evening but says alerts for the Thursday and Friday storms are likely. It issues these up to 48 hours ahead.

item.title: Investigation after Feyenoord fans set off fireworks at Cambuur
item.description:
Investigation after Feyenoord fans set off fireworks at Cambuur

August 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch football association KNVB will review its rules for dealing with disturbances at matches after five supporters were injured when fireworks were set off during Cambuur Leeuwarden’s home game against Feyenoord at the weekend.

Referee Danny Makkelie restarted the match in the De Kooi stadium after a 20-minute break, but questioned afterwards whether the guidelines should be changed.

At least one Cambuur fan suffered an eye injury while others had burns and hearing loss when Feyenoord fans let off a barrage of flares and fireworks in the 12th minute of the game. It is not known how the fireworks got into the stadium.

One firework landed at the feet of Feyenoord’s goalkeeper, Tjark Ernst, but he was unhurt. The current guidelines state that a match should be abandoned if a player is struck by fireworks, but say nothing about supporters.

“I asked the KNVB twice whether supporters being hit counted or not,” Makkelie told ESPN. Acting mayor Foort van Oosten instructed the referee to restart the game after consulting police.

“It’s an agreement made between the clubs, not us,” Makkelie explained. “I don’t know what the reason for it is, because it’s just as bad whether players or supporters are hit.”

Face coverings

Police were unable to arrest the culprits on the spot because the suspects were wearing balaclavas and their faces were obscured in the smoke. Efforts to identify them are continuing.

The KNVB will discuss the incident during its regular review meeting later this week.

When the game finally restarted, Feyenoord put their hosts to the sword, racing to a 4-0 lead by half-time, with Gjivai Zechiel opening the scoring in the 17th minute and Ayase Ueda bagging a penalty just before the break.

Cambuur pulled two goals back after the interval as Feyenoord eased off, before Zechiel’s second condemned the Frisian side to a third successive defeat.

PSV comeback

Groningen, who started the weekend as joint Eredivisie leaders, briefly threatened an upset in Eindhoven when Brynjolfur Willumsson gave them an early lead against PSV.

But the champions hit back, Ruben van Bommel causing mayhem down the left flank as PSV ran out 5-1 winners, with Croatian veteran Ivan Perisic scoring twice.

AZ Alkmaar are the only team with maximum points after three games after beating Fortuna Sittard 2-0 in Limburg.

The home side were reduced to 10 men after just four minutes when Ole Romney was sent off for stamping on Mateo Chávez. AZ struggled to make their advantage count, but Leeroy Echteld’s half-time substitutions proved decisive as Calvin Stengs twice set up Jizz Hornkamp for the goals.

PEC break duck

PEC Zwolle picked up their first points of the season by winning 2-0 at Heerenveen, but ADO Den Haag are still waiting after going down 3-1 at Go Ahead Eagles, who rose to second place in the table.

In Rotterdam, Sparta came back three times against Utrecht to claim a point and leave new manger Anthony Correia still looking for his first win. Defender Nick Verschuren scored the final equaliser in the 96th minute for Sparta.

Ajax, Twente and NEC Nijmegen were all allowed to reschedule their matches because of their European commitments in midweek.
